question: Which payment model requires a patient to pay the full cost right at the moment of receiving treatment?

options.A: National health insurance
options.B: Donor funding grants
options.C: Cooperative risk pools
options.D: User fees

explanation: User fees are paid straight out of pocket by the patient right at the point of service delivery. It's a very common system, though tough on families during emergencies!

question: What is a very common cause of acute (short-term) fatigue?

options.A: A recent viral infection or short-term sleep loss
options.B: Long-standing, unmanaged hypothyroidism
options.C: Advanced autoimmune joint destruction
options.D: A multi-year history of clinical depression

explanation: Exactly! Acute fatigue usually pops up suddenly from something clear and temporary, like fighting off a cold or pulling a late-night reading session for exams.

question: What is the main job of a midwife in a primary health care clinic?

options.A: Managing normal pregnancies and conducting safe deliveries
options.B: Treating chronic heart diseases in elderly patients
options.C: Performing routine dental extractions for children
options.D: Managing hospital financial accounts and budgets

explanation: You nailed it! Midwives are experts at caring for women through pregnancy and labor, ensuring both mother and baby come through safely.

question: A home health nurse visits a patient with chronic heart failure. Which action best supports long-term disease management?

options.A: Advising the patient to eat as much salted food as they want
options.B: Telling the patient to stop taking all prescribed daily water pills
options.C: Teaching the patient how to weigh themselves daily and track swelling
options.D: Discharging the patient from care because the disease is ongoing

explanation: Daily weight tracking helps catch fluid retention early before it turns into a dangerous heart failure flare-up. [learn more](GNS324_U1_T8#GNS324_U1_T8_h2)

question: Which international organization has the main global job of protecting and helping refugees?

options.A: UNESCO
options.B: FIFA
options.C: OPEC
options.D: UNHCR

explanation: The United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees (UNHCR) leads the charge globally in safeguarding refugees and finding long-term solutions for displaced people.

question: A newly admitted resident is very quiet and refuses to interact with others. What should the nurse do first?

options.A: Immediately discharge the resident back home for family care
options.B: Prescribe a mild sedative medication to calm their anxiety
options.C: Ignore the behavior since adjustment to a new home takes weeks
options.D: Conduct a comprehensive holistic assessment including psychological and social history

explanation: Spot on! Before jumping to conclusions, a warm, thorough assessment helps us find out if they are dealing with depression or fear so we can support them properly.

question: Why are Class IV drugs effective for treating supraventricular tachycardia?

options.A: They completely eliminate all electrical activity in the heart wall
options.B: They speed up the natural pacemaker cells in the right atrium
options.C: They slow down conduction through the atrioventricular node
options.D: They force the ventricles to beat faster than the upper chambers

explanation: By slowing AV node conduction, these drugs break the rapid loop causing supraventricular tachycardia. [learn more](GNS223_U1_T3#GNS223_U1_T3_h6)

question: What type of leadership style involves inviting input from team members before making decisions?

options.A: Democratic leadership
options.B: Bureaucratic leadership
options.C: Laissez-faire leadership
options.D: Autocratic leadership

explanation: Democratic leaders encourage participation and value input from the entire team when planning or solving problems. [learn more](GNS124_U5_T13#GNS124_U5_T13_h3)

question: What is the primary purpose of mechanical digestion?

options.A: To change proteins directly into amino acids
options.B: To neutralize stomach acid before food enters the bowel
options.C: To transport nutrients through the intestinal wall
options.D: To increase the surface area of food for enzymes

explanation: Mechanical digestion breaks food into smaller pieces, which gives digestive enzymes more surface area to work on. [learn more](GNS121_U1_T6#GNS121_U1_T6_h1)

question: When the sympathetic nervous system kicks in during stress, what happens to your digestion?

options.A: It has no effect on the gut
options.B: It increases gastric acid output
options.C: It stimulates pancreatic enzyme release
options.D: It decreases digestive secretions

explanation: Think of the 'fight or flight' response—your body focuses on survival, not digesting food, so digestive secretions slow right down. You've got this! [learn more](GNS121_U1_T12#GNS121_U1_T12_h1)

question: Why do dietitians need to understand human behavior along with food science?

options.A: Food chemistry changes completely based on the patient's mood
options.B: Patients need to feel understood in their cultural and personal habits to follow meal plans
options.C: Biochemical data alone is enough to change eating habits permanently
options.D: Psychological evaluations are legally required before writing a hospital diet

explanation: Knowing the science of food is only half the battle! If a patient's personal or cultural beliefs clash with the diet, they won't be able to follow it.

question: Why should you wash your hands right after taking off your mask?

options.A: To reactivate hand sanitizer lotions
options.B: To remove germs that may have touched your hands if you brushed the outer mask
options.C: To prevent mask elastic from marking your fingers
options.D: To cool your skin down after a long shift

explanation: Hand hygiene right after removal breaks the chain of infection just in case your fingers brushed against outer germs.

question: How does child health directly improve when a family uses effective family planning methods?

options.A: The need for childhood immunizations is drastically reduced.
options.B: Children automatically develop stronger natural immunity to all infections.
options.C: Infants are born with a higher average birth weight without exception.
options.D: Resources can be better shared to prevent malnutrition and infant illness.

explanation: You got it! When births are well-spaced, parents can better invest time, money, and nutrition into each child, keeping them healthier and well-nourished.

question: A nurse wipes down a bedside table between patients using a germicide. What level of cleaning is this?

options.A: Pasteurization
options.B: Disinfection
options.C: Sterilization
options.D: Antisepsis

explanation: Wiping down furniture and non-critical surfaces is disinfection. It gets rid of harmful germs without needing to destroy stubborn spores.

question: Which medication class is used long-term to lower uric acid production in the body?

options.A: Opioid analgesics like morphine
options.B: Xanthine oxidase inhibitors like allopurinol
options.C: Inhaled beta-agonists like albuterol
options.D: Loop diuretics like furosemide

explanation: Drugs like allopurinol block the enzyme that makes uric acid, helping keep future crystal build-up under control.

question: Why must you check a patient's kidney function before they get an injection of contrast dye?

options.A: Contrast dye increases the daily urine output significantly
options.B: Poor kidney function prevents the dye from reaching the joints
options.C: Kidneys must filter the dye to make bones show up white
options.D: Contrast dye can be toxic to the kidneys if clearance is slow

explanation: The kidneys have to filter out contrast dye. If a patient's kidneys aren't working well, the dye can linger and cause kidney damage, so checking lab results first is a crucial nursing duty.

question: What is the main reason for doing a community diagnosis?

options.A: To increase hospital admission rates across the state
options.B: To understand root causes of health issues and plan interventions
options.C: To replace individual clinical nursing practice completely
options.D: To punish local leaders for poor environmental sanitation

explanation: Exactly! Just like checking a patient's vitals before giving medicine, a community diagnosis helps you find the root problem so you can plan the right solution.

question: Why do patients with chronic hookworm infections often develop anemia?

options.A: Suppression of bone marrow by parasite toxins
options.B: Rapid destruction of red blood cells by the liver
options.C: A complete lack of dietary protein intake
options.D: Ongoing blood loss from intestinal attachment

explanation: Hookworms latch onto the inside of the intestines and feed on the host's blood. Over time, this steady loss adds up and leads to anemia. Makes total sense when you picture it!

question: Which diagnostic test directly checks the strength and status of a patient's immune system?

options.A: Urinalysis for protein
options.B: CD4+ T-cell count
options.C: Electrocardiogram (ECG)
options.D: Liver enzyme panel

explanation: Correct! The CD4+ count is our go-to test to see how many helper cells a patient has left to fight infections.

question: A patient cuts their forearm badly, damaging a major peripheral nerve, but months later sensation and movement return. What structure made this recovery possible?

options.A: Microglia replacing damaged muscle fibers
options.B: Oligodendrocytes wrapping the peripheral injury
options.C: Astrocytes migrating out of the spinal cord
options.D: Schwann cells forming a regeneration tube

explanation: In the peripheral nervous system, surviving Schwann cells rally together to form a pathway or 'tube' that guides the regrowing nerve back to where it belongs.

question: Which hormone gets released when fats and proteins show up in the small intestine?

options.A: Cholecystokinin
options.B: Aldosterone
options.C: Erythropoietin
options.D: Insulin

explanation: Cholecystokinin (let's just call it CCK!) is the hormone that shouts to the gallbladder and pancreas: 'Hey, fatty food has arrived, time to release your juices!'

question: Which of the following is part of routine safety monitoring for someone on long-term ARVs?

options.A: Performing a daily chest X-ray to look for bone fractures
options.B: Repeating HIV testing every single week to see if the virus is gone
options.C: Checking kidney and liver function tests regularly alongside clinical screenings
options.D: Checking the patient's blood pressure only when they report chest pain

explanation: Well done! Since ARVs are processed by the body over years, we run periodic liver and kidney lab tests to catch any organ strain early.

question: What is the main nitrogen waste product created when the body breaks down protein?

options.A: Urea
options.B: Sodium
options.C: Calcium
options.D: Glucose

explanation: Protein metabolism naturally produces nitrogen waste, which the liver turns into urea for the kidneys to excrete. [learn more](GNS227_U6_T004#GNS227_U6_T004_h2)

question: What is the traditional foundation for caring for the sick and elderly in Nigerian society?

options.A: Missionary parish health outposts
options.B: The extended family system
options.C: State-run geriatric nursing homes
options.D: Private commercial health agencies

explanation: In our culture, we lean heavily on extended family members to look after and support older or sick relatives at home. Beautiful tradition!

question: How does naloxone work so quickly to reverse an opioid overdose?

options.A: By competing for and blocking opioid receptor sites
options.B: By destroying the opioid molecules in the stomach
options.C: By coating the lining of the lungs to block absorption
options.D: By stimulating the kidneys to filter out the drug faster

explanation: Think of naloxone as a master key that pushes the opioid out of the lock (the receptor) and takes its place, instantly waking up the breathing center!

question: What is required before a human participant can take part in a research study?

options.A: A signed agreement to work on the ward
options.B: Voluntary informed consent
options.C: Approval from hospital accountants
options.D: Payment of a research fee

explanation: Ethics first! Participants must fully understand what the study involves and willingly agree to join without any pressure.

question: As a nurse caring for an adolescent struggling with substance use, which of these should you NOT do?

options.A: Connecting the family with professional counseling services
options.B: Establishing a respectful therapeutic relationship
options.C: Scolding the patient publicly for poor life choices
options.D: Providing accurate and realistic health education

explanation: Well done! As nurses, we always keep our care professional and non-judgmental—never shaming or scolding our patients.

question: Why is building trust with the community so vital during an Ebola outbreak?

options.A: It stops the virus from becoming airborne
options.B: It lets the government cancel travel bans
options.C: It prevents families from hiding sick relatives and encourages early reporting
options.D: It gives clinic staff higher pay

explanation: Correct! When people trust health workers, they bring sick family members in early instead of hiding them, which stops the spread.

question: How do SGLT2 inhibitor medications help lower your blood glucose?

options.A: By increasing the sensitivity of muscle receptors to circulating insulin
options.B: By stopping the liver from producing any new glucose molecules
options.C: By blocking renal glucose reabsorption and causing excretion in urine
options.D: By stimulating the pancreas to release extra insulin after meals

explanation: You nailed it! These drugs stop your kidneys from reabsorbing filtered sugar, so the extra glucose simply passes out through your urine.

question: What is the main reason hospitals require strict paperwork when disposing of damaged or expired drugs?

options.A: To prove to the government how many patients refused their treatment
options.B: To maintain a clear audit trail and prevent illegal drug diversion
options.C: To ensure pharmaceutical companies pay for the hospital water bills
options.D: To calculate exact bonuses for the hospital cleaning department

explanation: Proper records ensure that drugs marked as 'destroyed' aren't secretly slipping out into illegal markets. Accountability keeps everyone safe!

question: Lower national fertility rates are most directly associated with which public health outcome?

options.A: Guaranteed longevity past one hundred years of age
options.B: The elimination of chronic non-communicable illnesses
options.C: Complete eradication of all infectious diseases
options.D: Reduced maternal and child mortality burdens

explanation: Fewer high-risk pregnancies translate to fewer maternal and infant deaths, easing the strain on public health systems. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T002#GNS226_U6_T002_h5)

question: Which symptom is most common in perinatal anxiety disorders during pregnancy?

options.A: Sudden temporary loss of long-term memory
options.B: Complete indifference toward the entire pregnancy process
options.C: Physical weight gain without any emotional changes
options.D: Excessive, hard-to-control worry about the baby's health

explanation: Correct! Perinatal anxiety often looks like persistent, overwhelming fear and worry regarding the baby's safety.

question: Which behavior is very common for a patient dealing with illness anxiety?

options.A: Consistently ignoring all physical pain without worry
options.B: Repeatedly checking the body for lumps or abnormalities
options.C: Voluntarily stopping all interactions with healthcare workers
options.D: Seeking immediate surgery for nonexistent conditions

explanation: You will often see patients engage in compulsive checking—like constantly scanning their skin, checking their pulse, or probing for swollen lymph nodes.

question: What is the first step a nurse should take when counseling a client on family planning?

options.A: Choose a contraceptive method for the client without asking questions
options.B: Lecture the client on the economic dangers of large families
options.C: Refer the client immediately to a surgeon for sterilization
options.D: Assess the client's medical history and reproductive goals

explanation: Safe and effective counseling must begin with understanding the individual client's health background and personal preferences. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T002#GNS226_U6_T002_h6)

question: Why do food safety officers frequently inspect local open-air markets and street food vendors?

options.A: These vendors feed a huge portion of the urban working-class population
options.B: Street vendors have more money to pay official fines
options.C: Open markets never have contamination problems
options.D: Large supermarkets are legally exempt from all safety checks

explanation: Since millions of people buy from local markets and street vendors every day, keeping those foods safe is crucial for public health.

question: How should a nurse approach dietary counselling with a patient?

options.A: An ongoing, continuous process
options.B: A purely administrative paperwork duty
options.C: A one-time hospital lecture
options.D: A task completed only upon discharge

explanation: Spot on! Nutrition is a journey, not a one-time lecture. We check in, encourage, and make adjustments as the patient heals. [learn more](GNS227_U7_T005#GNS227_U7_T005_h7)

question: Why do nurses check both central pulses and listen to the chest when confirming death?

options.A: To stimulate the nervous system into restarting
options.B: To measure the exact blood pressure before the body cools
options.C: To ensure absolute certainty that circulation has ceased
options.D: To determine which chamber of the heart failed first

explanation: Spot on! Using a couple of different checks removes any doubt and gives you a clear picture.

question: What is the standard bedside scale nurses use to quickly check a trauma patient's level of consciousness?

options.A: Braden Scale
options.B: Pain Numeric Rating
options.C: Apgar Score
options.D: Glasgow Coma Scale

explanation: You nailed it! The Glasgow Coma Scale (GCS) checks eye, verbal, and motor responses so we can quickly tell how alert or responsive a patient is.

question: Why is an injection considered a high-risk procedure despite its daily frequency?

options.A: It requires specialized surgical equipment to perform safely
options.B: It bypasses the body's natural skin barrier and enters sterile tissues directly
options.C: It is the only medical procedure that causes severe allergic reactions
options.D: It is always performed in emergency situations without preparation

explanation: Because a needle breaks the skin, any contamination on the equipment or technique introduces pathogens straight into the body, bypassing primary defenses. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T2#GNS122_U3_T2_h1)

question: What happens to the length of thin and thick filaments during muscle contraction?

options.A: They stretch out to make the muscle longer
options.B: They shorten significantly as the muscle contracts
options.C: They dissolve completely and reform afterward
options.D: They slide past each other and stay the same length

explanation: The sliding filament theory states that filaments do not change length; they simply overlap more as they slide past each other. [learn more](GNS121_U3_T9#GNS121_U3_T9_h4)

question: What is the absolute number one priority when managing a patient with a suspected drug overdose?

options.A: Securing the airway and ensuring breathing
options.B: Administering a laxative to clear the bowels
options.C: Finding out the exact name of the drug taken
options.D: Filling out the hospital admission forms

explanation: Remember your ABCs! In any emergency, stabilizing the airway, breathing, and circulation always comes before playing detective to find out what happened.

question: A patient comes in with ringworm, a skin condition that loves warm and damp places. Which class of pathogen is causing this?

options.A: Bacterium
options.B: Protozoa
options.C: Fungus
options.D: Virus

explanation: Fungi love warm, humid places (just like our weather sometimes!). They are notorious for causing superficial skin issues like ringworm and athlete's foot.

question: Why is it important for nurses to report both real vaccine reactions and random health events that happen after vaccination?

options.A: To prove that pharmaceutical manufacturing companies are always at fault for patient illness
options.B: To automatically trigger immediate free hospital admission for every sick child
options.C: To help health authorities investigate and determine the true root cause of the incident
options.D: To legally punish mothers who bring their children late for routine clinic appointments

explanation: Reporting helps public health experts look at the facts, figure out what really happened, and keep immunization safe for everyone.

question: A home health nurse notices a normally active toddler has become unusually quiet and lethargic. What should the nurse do first?

options.A: Perform a focused physical assessment and check vital signs
options.B: Tell the parents to change the child's diet immediately
options.C: Wait until the scheduled weekly visit to mention it to the doctor
options.D: Assume the child is just sleepy and leave the home

explanation: Spot on! Any sudden change in behavior needs a quick, careful check to catch early signs of a worsening condition. [learn more](GNS324_U3_T11#GNS324_U3_T11_h3)

question: Which of these is a major reason why chronic venous insufficiency happens?

options.A: Damaged, weak valves that let blood pool in the legs
options.B: Muscles in the deep veins going into painful spasms
options.C: High pressure from arteries bursting the capillaries
options.D: Fast plaque buildup inside the surface veins

explanation: When venous valves get tired or damaged and fail to close tightly, gravity pulls the blood down, causing it to pool in the lower legs. You're learning fast!

question: Which muscle is a safe, standard site for giving an intramuscular DMPA injection?

options.A: Gastrocnemius muscle
options.B: Ventrogluteal muscle
options.C: Rectus abdominis muscle
options.D: Internal oblique muscle

explanation: The ventrogluteal site is a fantastic choice because it has a thick muscle mass safely away from major nerves and blood vessels.

question: A patient complains of a stubborn dry cough two weeks after starting a new blood pressure pill. As a nurse, what should you do first?

options.A: Tell the patient to stop taking all medications immediately without telling anyone
options.B: Document the symptom and report it as a suspected adverse drug reaction
options.C: Ignore the complaint because coughs are unrelated to blood pressure drugs
options.D: Prescribe an over-the-counter cough syrup for the patient to use daily

explanation: Great clinical judgment! Always note down the change, discuss it with the team, and report it using the proper channels like the Yellow Form.

question: Why are gonadotropin fertility hormones usually given as injections instead of swallowing pills?

options.A: Pills would cause too much stomach upset
options.B: Protein-based hormones are destroyed in the digestive tract
options.C: Injections are cheaper to manufacture
options.D: Injections allow patients to self-dose without a prescription

explanation: Hormones like FSH are proteins that would be broken down and ruined by stomach acid if swallowed as pills. Makes total sense!

question: Why is sterilization stricter and more powerful than standard disinfection?

options.A: It only applies to items that touch intact human skin
options.B: It can be completed in a few seconds using simple wipes
options.C: It targets and kills bacterial spores as well as vegetative cells
options.D: It is performed using mild soaps and warm running water

explanation: Disinfection kills a lot of germs, but tough bacterial spores can survive it. Sterilization goes the extra mile to destroy those resilient spores completely!

question: A patient with advanced terminal cervical cancer is in severe, constant pain in her pelvis and back. What is your top nursing priority?

options.A: Preparing the patient for emergency radical pelvic surgery
options.B: Encouraging the patient to walk outside to distract her from the pain
options.C: Administering prescribed analgesics regularly based on pain assessment
options.D: Restricting fluid intake to decrease pressure on the pelvic organs

explanation: You've got it. In palliative care, keeping the patient comfortable through regular, structured pain relief is a top priority to preserve their dignity and quality of life.

question: What fluid is found mainly inside the inner ear's membranous labyrinth?

options.A: Cerebrospinal fluid
options.B: Blood plasma
options.C: Perilymph
options.D: Endolymph

explanation: Endolymph is the special fluid that fills the inner compartments of the labyrinth to help us sense movement. [learn more](GNS211_U4_T8#GNS211_U4_T8_h2)

question: Why should newly hired nurses be introduced to the hospital's cultural values during orientation?

options.A: To discourage them from asking senior staff members for clinical help
options.B: To ensure they adopt expected behaviours and maintain the positive environment
options.C: To test their ability to memorize complex hospital administration bylaws
options.D: To reduce the amount of orientation salary the hospital has to pay them

explanation: Spot on! Early orientation helps new nurses fit right into the positive workplace culture, keeping standards of teamwork and safety high.

question: What does 'exclusive breastfeeding' mean for a baby during their first six months?

options.A: Combining breast milk with small amounts of clean water
options.B: Receiving breast milk supplemented with medicinal teas
options.C: Receiving only breast milk with no other foods or liquids
options.D: Alternating daily feeds between formula and breast milk

explanation: Spot on! Exclusive breastfeeding means absolutely nothing else by mouth except breast milk and any prescribed medicines.

question: What is the medical word for bone marrow slowing down due to chemotherapy?

options.A: Hyperglycemia
options.B: Splenomegaly
options.C: Vasoconstriction
options.D: Myelosuppression

explanation: You got it! 'Myelo' means bone marrow, and 'suppression' means slowing down. It means fewer blood cells are being made.

question: Why is 'mixed feeding' (giving both breast milk and other foods or liquids) so risky for a baby born to an HIV-positive mum?

options.A: It completely stops the mother's breast milk production overnight
options.B: It causes immediate allergic reactions in the newborn stomach
options.C: It damages the gut lining and increases the risk of viral transmission
options.D: It neutralizes the protective effect of infant antiretroviral syrups

explanation: Mixing feeds irritates a baby's tiny, developing gut, creating tiny gaps that make it much easier for the virus in breast milk to enter their bloodstream.

question: What is the main goal of the preliminary stage in wastewater treatment?

options.A: Killing all microscopic bacteria using chlorine gas
options.B: Adding oxygen to stimulate helpful aerobic microbes
options.C: Filtering out dissolved chemical salts and heavy metals
options.D: Removing large physical objects like plastics and rags

explanation: You got it! Before treating water, we have to screen out big trash like nylons and plastics so they don't break the treatment machinery.

question: Which of these means a planned home birth is definitely NOT safe?

options.A: Single fetus in cephalic presentation
options.B: Strong personal desire for home birth
options.C: Previous cesarean section delivery
options.D: Spontaneous onset of labor at term

explanation: Spot on. A uterus with a scar from a past CS has a risk of tearing during labor, so a hospital setting is much safer.

question: Why do nurses need to understand the basics of where our food comes from?

options.A: Many chronic health issues and nutritional deficiencies originate in the food system
options.B: Nurses are required to inspect commercial farms daily
options.C: Hospital kitchens are managed directly by nursing staff
options.D: Nurses must calculate the exact cost of groceries for patients

explanation: You'll see many patients dealing with malnutrition or diet-related illnesses, and tracing it back starts with understanding how food is grown and processed.

question: Why is keeping a close eye on fluids and electrolytes a top nursing priority for enteric fever patients?

options.A: Fluid intake increases the growth rate of bacteria
options.B: Persistent high fevers and diarrhea can quickly lead to severe dehydration
options.C: Patients are forbidden from drinking water
options.D: Antibiotics automatically cause total kidney failure

explanation: You got it! Fever and tummy upsets make patients lose water fast, so monitoring hydration is a core nursing duty.

question: Which patients should receive standard precautions in the hospital?

options.A: Patients admitted to surgical wards only
options.B: Only patients with confirmed viral infections
options.C: Every patient in the healthcare facility
options.D: Individuals with active pulmonary tuberculosis

explanation: Exactly! Standard precautions are universal. Treat every patient as if their body fluids could carry infection, keeping both them and yourself protected.

question: Which of these is one of the most common causes of nursing malpractice claims?

options.A: Failing to attend annual hospital parties
options.B: Forgetting to log into the electronic health record on time
options.C: Medication administration errors
options.D: Refusing to work mandatory overtime shifts

explanation: Giving the wrong drug, wrong dose, or missing a route can easily harm a patient. This is why our 5 rights of medication administration are drilled into us!

question: Which common hormonal condition is a frequent cause of chronic anovulation and irregular periods?

options.A: Polycystic ovary syndrome
options.B: Gestational diabetes mellitus
options.C: Uterine leiomyoma or fibroids
options.D: Acute pelvic inflammatory disease

explanation: Polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS) throws off the usual hormonal balance, making it tricky for the ovaries to regularly select and release a dominant follicle.

question: What is the main job of a research question in a nursing study?

options.A: To increase the total word count of the research report
options.B: To replace the need for a formal literature review
options.C: To guide every step of the study from start to finish
options.D: To prove that the researcher's opinion is correct

explanation: Think of a research question like a map or a compass. It keeps your literature review, data collection, and methods pointing in the exact right direction!

question: Why do nurses join trade unions and professional associations?

options.A: To replace hospital managers and run the finance department
options.B: To diagnose patients without consulting medical doctors
options.C: To collectively advocate for better working conditions and pay
options.D: To bypass the need for government health laws completely

explanation: Unions give workers collective bargaining power to demand fair wages, safety gear, and reasonable hours. [learn more](GST321_U6_T3#GST321_U6_T3_h6)

question: What is a common risk when a patient is placed on a soft diet for a long period?

options.A: Rapid muscle building
options.B: Severe high blood pressure
options.C: Decreased appetite and weight loss
options.D: Sudden increase in bone density

explanation: Because soft foods can look less appetizing, patients often eat less, putting them at risk for poor nutrition and weight loss. [learn more](GNS227_U6_T002#GNS227_U6_T002_h6)

question: During a suspected outbreak of an animal-borne disease, what is a key role for a nurse?

options.A: Manufacturing new chemical pesticides in a hospital laboratory
options.B: Reporting suspected cases and educating the community on prevention
options.C: Enforcing quarantine laws through police and military patrols
options.D: Designing blueprints for modern municipal drainage systems

explanation: You got it! Nurses are right on the front lines, helping catch outbreaks early and teaching people how to stay safe.

question: In type 1 diabetes, which part of the body does the immune system mistakenly attack?

options.A: The lining of the small intestine
options.B: Insulin-producing beta cells in the pancreas
options.C: The protective sheaths around nerves
options.D: The membranes lining major joints

explanation: Type 1 diabetes is a classic autoimmune condition where the body turns on its own pancreas, destroying the beta cells that make insulin. Brilliant connection to remember!

question: A patient is recovering from deep skin wounds. Why is giving them extra protein so important?

options.A: To supply essential fatty acids for nerve insulation
options.B: To accelerate tissue regeneration and close wounds
options.C: To provide a quick surge of energy for walking
options.D: To prevent the kidneys from retaining too much fluid

explanation: Proteins are the body's chief repair crew. When there are wounds or burns to heal, the body needs extra protein to build new tissue and close the skin.

question: A charge nurse creates the weekly duty roster and assigns patient loads for the morning shift. What type of plan is this?

options.A: Strategic plan
options.B: Visionary plan
options.C: Operational plan
options.D: Tactical plan

explanation: Duty rosters and daily patient assignments are classic examples of short-term operational planning at the unit level. [learn more](GST321_U1_T6#GST321_U1_T6_h4)

question: What is the main benefit of using hydrotherapy (water exercise) in rehab?

options.A: Water buoyancy reduces joint stress during physical exercise.
options.B: It replaces the need for any nutritional support.
options.C: It eliminates all risks of secondary skin infections.
options.D: It completely cures chronic neurological disorders in days.

explanation: Well done! The water helps support the patient's weight, taking pressure off painful or weak joints so they can move more easily.

question: A patient develops cor pulmonale from chronic lung disease. What sign might you spot as a nurse?

options.A: A sudden spike in blood glucose levels
options.B: Sudden sharp chest pain and absent breath sounds
options.C: Bright red blood coming up when coughing
options.D: Swollen lower legs and distended neck veins

question: A clinic pharmacy is running out of cash because staff members keep taking drugs on credit and rarely pay. What should management do?

question: What is the main reason why hospitals and wards have policies?

options.D: To increase the cost of purchasing medical supplies

question: Why do we need a whole team of different specialists for cancer rehab?

options.A: The physical and emotional needs of survivors are too diverse for one discipline
options.B: It lowers the overall cost of hospital administration
options.C: Hospital rules require multiple signatures for every session

question: What exactly is a perineal laceration when a woman is giving birth?

options.C: A surgical cut made by a doctor to widen the birth canal

question: A patient having an autoimmune flare has extreme fatigue and stiff joints. What is a great initial nursing action?

options.B: Help the patient plan daily activities and schedule mandatory rest periods
options.C: Advise the patient to stop taking all prescribed medications immediately
options.D: Encourage the patient to push through the fatigue with rigorous exercise

question: If a researcher labels 'Male' as 1 and 'Female' as 2 in a survey, what is this step called?

options.D: Cleaning

question: Why would an educator use parallel forms reliability for a student exam?

question: What is the main difference between skilled care and custodial care?

options.A: Skilled care requires licensed health professionals for complex medical needs.

options.C: Custodial care requires advanced clinical judgment and monitoring.

question: Which of these is NOT a common physical barrier for people with disabilities in public buildings?

options.A: Wide automatic sliding entrance doors
options.B: Absence of functional elevators in multi-story buildings
options.C: Narrow doorways that block wheelchairs
options.D: High staircases without accompanying ramps

question: Why did early healers perform trephining (drilling a hole in the skull) on people with mental illness?

options.A: To relieve increased pressure from a stroke
options.B: To allow trapped evil spirits to escape
options.C: To cure long-standing chronic migraines

question: Which triage category is meant for a patient who needs life-saving help right this second?

options.A: Resuscitation
options.B: Urgent

options.D: Routine

question: What is the nurse's main job when assessing a patient's diet?

options.B: Prescribing strict hospital therapeutic diets
options.C: Collecting and evaluating food intake data
options.D: Purchasing nutritional supplements for wards

explanation: You've got this! Nurses gather information on what patients eat to spot any nutrition risks early and plan the best care possible.

question: What is the top priority for a nurse caring for a patient right after surgery in the recovery room?

options.A: Obtaining the signed surgical consent form from the family
options.B: Assisting the surgeon with closing skin incisions in theater
options.C: Monitoring airway patency, breathing, and vital signs
options.D: Discussing long-term dietary changes for home care

explanation: Airway and breathing always come first! In recovery (PACU), keeping those airways clear and vitals stable is your number one life-saving duty.

question: A nurse uses a dietary assessment to establish a baseline. What does this mean for patient care?

options.A: It provides a starting point to measure future nutritional changes and treatment progress
options.B: It acts as a permanent record that cannot be altered during the hospital stay
options.C: It proves that the patient has no underlying metabolic diseases
options.D: It serves as the final clearance for the patient to be discharged home

explanation: Establishing a baseline gives healthcare providers a reference point to see if interventions are helping or if the patient's condition is worsening. [learn more](GNS227_U5_T002#GNS227_U5_T002_h2)

question: Which of these is NOT a common barrier stopping women from using post-abortion contraception?

options.A: Fear of unpleasant side effects
options.B: Lack of transport to the clinic
options.C: Guaranteed 100 percent long-term effectiveness
options.D: High product costs at the pharmacy

question: A patient has an overdose of a weak acid medication. What clinical action helps clear the drug faster?

options.A: Acidifying the urine with specific supplements
options.B: Restricting oral fluid intake to concentrate the urine
options.C: Alkalinizing the urine with sodium bicarbonate
options.D: Giving large doses of intravenous fat emulsions

question: Why should nurses never use ordinary kitchen spoons to measure out liquid medicines?

options.A: Liquid medications will stain metal spoons permanently
options.B: Hospital policy strictly forbids touching any utensil from a kitchen
options.C: Plastic spoons react chemically with syrup and destroy the drug
options.D: Household spoons vary widely in size and do not provide accurate doses

explanation: Spot on! Kitchen spoons come in all shapes and sizes, which can easily lead to giving too much or too little medicine.

question: In the SMART framework for setting goals, what does the letter 'M' stand for?

options.A: Meaningful

options.C: Mandatory
options.D: Managed

explanation: 'M' is for Measurable! It means we include numbers or clear indicators so we can track our progress and see how well we are doing.

question: How does popular media often misrepresent sexual intercourse to teenagers?

options.A: As casual, glamorous, and rarely involving negative consequences

options.C: As something that only occurs among older adults
options.D: As an event that always results in immediate health complications

question: An ICU patient is intubated and fighting the breathing machine. What is the doctor most likely to order?

options.A: Administering a continuous sedative infusion to calm the central nervous system

options.C: Providing a strong stimulant medication to increase lung capacity
options.D: Applying topical anesthetic cream directly to the chest wall

explanation: Sedatives help keep critical care patients comfortable so they can rest easily on life support without fighting the ventilator. [learn more](GNS223_U6_T2#GNS223_U6_T2_h4)

question: Which of these is a key nursing action when assessing someone with a degenerative disease?

options.A: Prescribing new gene-therapy medications
options.B: Reversing the genetic mutation in the laboratory
options.C: Performing major orthopedic surgery
options.D: Evaluating motor strength and skin integrity

explanation: Spot on! As nurses, we keep a close watch on muscle strength, movement, and skin health to keep our patients as safe and comfortable as possible.

question: What is the main sign of complicated grief?

options.A: A normal, healthy reaction that resolves completely within two weeks

options.C: Intense grief symptoms that remain severe and debilitating long after the loss

explanation: You got it! Complicated grief happens when a person gets stuck in deep, unyielding pain that stops them from getting back to daily life.

question: What does the term 'countertransference' mean in nursing?

options.A: When the hospital administration changes a patient's care assignment
options.B: When the nurse projects personal feelings or unresolved issues onto the patient
options.C: When the patient projects feelings from past relationships onto the nurse
options.D: When communication breaks down due to language and cultural barriers

explanation: Countertransference happens when you accidentally let your own personal emotions, memories, or biases spill over onto how you treat a patient.

question: Why can the word 'erosion' be a bit confusing for this condition?

options.A: The condition only affects postmenopausal women
options.B: It always causes complete destruction of the cervix
options.C: The outer cells grow inward rather than outward
options.D: The tissue is not actually worn away or ulcerated

question: After making a solid plan for your ward, what is the very next step in the nursing management process?

options.A: Planning

question: Why is daily record keeping at local primary health clinics important for disease surveillance?

options.A: It proves to international donors that local nurses are working hard

question: What is the main goal of risk management in nursing?

options.A: Increasing the number of daily patient admissions

options.C: Punishing staff members who make clinical errors
options.D: Reducing the cost of hospital equipment purchases

explanation: You've got this! Risk management is all about keeping everyone in the hospital safe by spotting dangers early and stopping accidents before they happen.

question: What does the accessibility principle mean in youth-friendly health services?

options.A: Staff members must speak at least three local languages fluently

options.C: Healthcare workers must visit every school in the community monthly
options.D: Clinics must provide free medications for all chronic illnesses

question: What term describes the thinning of the cervix during the first stage of labor?

question: A client with severe difficulty swallowing (dysphagia) just finished a meal in bed. What is your most important immediate action?

options.B: Lay the client flat immediately to help with digestion
options.C: Keep the head of the bed elevated for at least 30 minutes

question: What is a primary responsibility of a nurse working in an assisted living facility?

options.A: Managing hospital emergency room admissions

options.D: Performing major surgical operations on-site

question: What happens when the lower oesophageal sphincter fails to close properly?

question: What is the primary reason for tracking down and treating the sexual partners of an infected patient?

options.A: To collect financial fines for public health registries
options.B: To prevent immediate reinfection of the original patient
options.C: To test the partners for unrelated chronic diseases
options.D: To ensure the partners report to police authorities

question: What is the correct way to store an epinephrine auto-injector?

options.A: Leave it inside a parked car during hot sunny days for easy access.

question: A pregnant woman at 32 weeks gestation arrives with vaginal bleeding and a rigid, painful abdomen. What is the most appropriate immediate nursing action?

question: What is the main benefit when a family practices subsistence farming?

question: When would you choose dry heat sterilization instead of an autoclave?

question: Why does the human body require a dual-circuit vascular system?

question: What is the biggest benefit of nurses and physical therapists working closely together?

question: Why might a patient have normal vital signs even when they are in severe pain?

question: Which symptom is most characteristic of circulatory overload during a blood transfusion?

question: What is the most important thing a nurse checks first during a cholera outbreak?

question: In many Nigerian clinical settings, what is a major hurdle that stops patients from getting their prescribed drugs?

question: You check a patient's lab results, like serum albumin and electrolytes. What type of nutritional data is this?

question: A patient with severe malaria isn't getting better despite finishing a full course of drugs bought from an unverified roadside vendor. What should you suspect?

question: What is the main clinical purpose of performing basic anthropometric measurements in a hospital?

question: What is a common trap nurses should avoid when a patient starts a new drug and develops a weird symptom?

question: Which gland produces melatonin to help control your sleep cycle?

question: When does a medication error cross the line from a civil mistake into criminal liability?

question: What is the rule regarding breast milk that has been frozen and then thawed for a feeding?

question: Which hormone surge directly triggers the release of an egg?

question: What usually triggers a flexor or withdrawal reflex?

question: Why do hospitals prefer phased construction plans over shutting down completely during expansions?

question: Which substance does the body overproduce during healing, leading to keloids?

question: What is the best move when a grateful patient offers you an expensive gift?

question: Why do we even need health care economics in our hospitals?

question: Why is keeping patients in prolonged physical restraints at some spiritual healing camps a major concern?

question: A nurse is talking to an overweight teenager about healthy eating. What is the most encouraging and effective approach?

question: What is the biggest advantage of using qualitative methods like focus group discussions?

question: Which factor is critical to maintain during the implementation of a health project?

question: Why is standardization especially critical for plant-derived medicines?
